title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of member States to ratify and apply international labour standards and to fulfil their reporting obligations

description.narrative:
The Office will continue to assist the government in aligning its legal frameworks with the latest international conventions, addressing any gaps, and actively considering the recommendations of the Supervisory Review Mechanism. Efforts will focus on developing and implementing a ratification plan, prioritizing gap assessments where needed. The government will be supported in organizing social partners and provincial counterparts to raise awareness on the importance of ratifying up-to-date conventions, positioning Pakistan as a responsible state and ethical business partner. For existing ratifications, the office will continue supporting the ILS reporting committees and the federal government in ensuring quality reports and responses to comments from the ILO’s supervisory mechanism. Additionally, the ILO will support legal reforms at the provincial level and facilitate collaboration among stakeholders and social partners in these areas.
Building on prior work in sectors like Better Work and ILES, the office will implement a code of practice on occupational safety and health (OSH) in textiles, clothing, leather, and footwear in selected textile mills in Karachi. It will also provide technical assistance in reviewing draft legislation and regulations on chemical use and management in these sectors, collaborating closely with the Ministry of Climate Change under the GEF/UNEP project to reduce chemical use, including persistent organic pollutants (POPs), in textiles.
In addition to the textiles sector, the office will implement other sectoral codes and tools in shipbreaking, sanitation, construction, and health, aiming to develop sector-specific initiatives throughout the country.
